newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jews to be detained ahead of Hebron redeployment.
newsitem.headline: Jews to be detained ahead of Hebron redeployment.

text.p: Israel will detain dozens of Jewish militants who might actively oppose a turnover of Hebron ahead of an Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town, an Israeli official said on Saturday.

Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani was speaking to Israel army radio as thousands of religious Jews gathered in Hebron for the annual reading of a biblical passage marking what they regard as their birthright to the town.

Asked about Jewish militants who oppose an Israeli troop withdrawal from most of the Hebron, Kahalani said: "We are preparing for a situation where extremists like this will open fire and will try to incite the flames.
"We are prepared for this situation and we will pick up those who are dangerous and endanger public life in the area and put them in some corner and take care of this matter."

Asked if he was referring to administrative detention orders which would allow security forces to imprison Jewish militants without trial, he said: "If we need to we will also do that. We have to prevent them from trying to incite the flames."

Security was heightened in the town as observant Jews from throughout Israel joined the 400-strong settler community for the reading of the Bible portion relating to patriarch Abraham's purchase of a burial area in Hebron for his wife Sarah.
The Tomb of the Patriarchs in Hebron, traditionally the site bought by Abraham, is now a complex revered by both Jews and Moslems. It is known to Moslems as the al-Ibrahimi mosque.
In February 1994 a Jewish militant from Kiryat Arba settlement adjacent to Hebron shot dead 29 Arabs at prayer in the mosque. He was beaten to death by survivors.
Israel and the PLO are currently locked in U.S.-brokered negotiations on implementing a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment from the town of 100,000 Palestinians.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the Likud party seeks to modify the Hebron deal signed by the previous Labour-led government to safeguard the settlers who live in the heart of the city. Palestinians reject any changes to the accord.
